customManagers.description: Commit of the upstream ESPHome project this integration was last compared with, see Upstream changes in docs/development.md. git-refs reads the branch head with git ls-remote.

packageRules.description: Tools pinned for CI and in .pre-commit-config.yaml move in one pull request so hook and CI cannot disagree, see docs/development.md.

New releases wait three days, so a compromised or withdrawn release is not proposed at once; security pull requests do not wait. Not for the hassfest and HACS actions (github-digest), so new validation rules arrive at once, nor for the upstream commits (git-refs), which have no release dates and would wait forever.
Major updates only after approval in the Dependency Dashboard issue.
Python minors are runtime changes and need approval too.

Home Assistant uses calendar versions, so the first release of a year is a major update without being a breaking one. Every stable release of the Home Assistant tests is proposed without approval, see Home Assistant tests in docs/development.md.

New upstream commits are a review task, not a pin bump: the pull request is the reminder to compare components/votronic_ble and transfer the changes, see Upstream changes in docs/development.md. Matched by depName because the custom manager sets the package name to the GitHub URL.
prBodyNotes: Follow `Upstream changes` in `docs/development.md`: transfer the changes to this pull request, or merge it as is when the commits do not touch `components/votronic_ble`.
